title: Source list vertices precede the instruction block
statement: Let $K$ be a nonempty set of instruction kinds, let $m,w,n$ be natural numbers, and let $F:K\to\{0,1\}^*\to\{0,1\}^*$ assign an output bit string to each kind and input bit string. A program is a finite list of instructions, each with a kind in $K$ and an ordered list of bit sources. For each kind $k$, let $W(k)$ be the sum, over the first $w$ output positions, of one plus the number of gates in the circuit compiled from the Boolean function giving that output bit of $F(k,\cdot)$ on $m$ input bits (an out-of-range output position is read as zero). For $i$ no greater than the program length, put $B_i=n+2+\sum_{r<i}W(k_r)$, where $k_r$ is the kind of instruction $r$. Form a list by mapping each source of instruction $i$ to its assigned vertex, appending $m$ copies of $n$, and retaining only the first $m$ entries. Every vertex in this list is strictly less than $B_i$.
hypotheses_covered: A nonempty set $K$ of instruction kinds
A function $F$ from kinds and input bit strings to output bit strings
A finite program of instructions with kinds and ordered bit sources
An index $i$ at most the program length
caveat: The statement depends on circuit gadgets and output-position offsets; these are described from their defining construction to make the bound self-contained.
